label: Amendment 3
what: Repeals the 2024 voter-approved constitutional right to reproductive health care, including abortion up to fetal viability. Allows abortion only for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, and rape or incest before 12 weeks; allows laws regulating abortion; requires parental consent for minors; and bans gender-transition surgery, cross-sex hormones and puberty blockers for minors.
y: Abortion is restricted to the listed exceptions and gender-transition procedures for minors are constitutionally banned.
n: The 2024 amendment stays, keeping abortion access through fetal viability.
fiscal: Official fiscal note summary: state entities estimate no costs or savings; Greene County estimates an unknown increase in tax revenue; other local entities estimate no costs or savings.
pro: Missouri Republican Party, U.S. Sen. Josh Hawley, Missouri Right to Life, Missouri Catholic Conference
con: Planned Parenthood Great Rivers Action, ACLU of Missouri, Abortion Action Missouri, League of Women Voters of Missouri, PROMO Missouri, SEIU MO/KS

label: Amendment 6
t: Protect citizen initiatives from legislative changes
what: Makes initiative and referendum rights 'fundamental rights' subject to strict scrutiny, bars the legislature from weakening them (e.g., raising signature thresholds or requiring supermajorities), and lets courts rewrite misleading ballot summaries. The legislature could change or repeal a voter-approved initiative only by an 80% vote of both chambers followed by voter approval. Keeps current signature and simple-majority requirements.
y: Voter-approved initiatives could be changed only with 80% legislative votes plus a public vote, and the initiative process is shielded from new limits.
n: The legislature can keep amending or repealing initiated statutes by ordinary law.
fiscal: Official fiscal note summary: state and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.
pro: Respect MO Voters, former U.S. Sen. John Danforth, Missouri AFL-CIO, Missouri NEA, Missouri NAACP, Show Me Integrity, Sierra Club Missouri

label: Amendment 7
t: Create 'Show-Me Prosperity' fund to replace state taxes
what: Creates a permanent state endowment, funded by legislative appropriations and gifts and invested by the treasurer in S&P 500 index funds. Nothing may be spent until yearly earnings are enough to replace state income, sales and corporate taxes; then up to 3% of the fund's five-year average value a year would be used solely to eliminate those taxes, which could not be re-enacted unless the fund fails.
y: The endowment is created, with the long-term goal of eliminating state taxes once its earnings are large enough.
fiscal: Official fiscal note summary: state and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings. Fair ballot language: no immediate impact on taxes, but could lead to elimination of state taxes if fund earnings become sufficient.
pro: Sen. Adam Schnelting (R, sponsor), Freedom Principle MO
con: No organised opposition; Cato Institute analyst Ted DeHaven criticised the approach

label: Amendment 8
t: Put elected county sheriffs in the constitution
what: Requires counties to elect a sheriff every four years (now required by statute), puts sheriffs' duties in the constitution, and allows an elected sheriff to be removed only through a quo warranto action brought by the Attorney General. St. Louis City, St. Louis County and St. Charles County are excepted.
y: Elected sheriffs and their duties are written into the constitution, with removal only by the Attorney General's quo warranto action.
n: Current statutes on electing sheriffs and their duties and removal remain and can be changed by law.
fiscal: Official fiscal note summary: state and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.

label: Proposition A
what: Asks whether to approve House Bill 1 (2025 special session), which replaced Missouri's 2022 congressional map with new districts that split Kansas City across several districts. Analysts say it gives Republicans an advantage in seven of eight districts, up from six. The 2022 map governs the November 2026 election either way.
n: HB 1 is repealed and the 2022 congressional map stays.
fiscal: Official fiscal note summary: state and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.
pro: (Yes) Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, Republican National Committee, NRCC, Put Missouri First
con: (No) People Not Politicians, Democratic National Committee, National Education Association, SEIU MO/KS, National Redistricting Action Fund
